answer: An agent marketplace can require each voting identity to lock $100 for 30 days, with one vote per deposit and no reuse of locked funds. An attacker can forge a thousand identities, but activating them ties up $100,000 for a month, costing liquidity and forgone interest. The market offers no free harbor for aliases: an agent called sparrow faces the same deposit rule as every other voter, so influence scales with committed capital.
